title: North Star Canvas
description: L1 North Star metric + input metrics + Goodhart guard. Permissive: type-pins established top-level keys. Added 2026-06-12 (gap analysis). Witnessed failure this schema's parse-layer would have caught: roadmap north-star.yml broken YAML 2026-05-23 (cluster instance 14).

metric.description: The North Star metric itself: name, definition, current value. `current_value` may carry a `source_ref` pointer (see `$defs/source_ref`) when the count lives in a file.

input_metrics.description: Leading input metrics that drive the North Star. Any value inside `current_value` may be written as `{source_ref: <pointer>, value: <cache>}` instead of a literal; see `$defs/source_ref`.

guardrails.description: Counter-metrics guarding against optimizing the North Star at the expense of health.

goodhart_check.description: Explicit Goodhart's-Law audit block: how this metric could be gamed and what watches for it.

source_ref.description: A DERIVED field (v0.218.0): a pointer to where the value lives, resolved at read time by check_derived_fields.py, instead of a transcribed copy. Forms: `metrics/<source>#<dotted.path>` (newest .claude/evals/metrics/<source>/*.json) or `<file>.yml#<dotted.path>[|count[ key=value]]` (a canvas, diamonds or harness file; the path walks keys, list indexes and item ids; `|count` counts a list, optionally filtered). A mapping may carry `value` beside it as a cache; the check reports every cache that disagrees with its source. Why: the dogfood canvas measured five hand-copied KPI drifts of 17 to 76 days, and the block carrying the sentence 'a KPI block hand-copied from a snapshot directory will keep rotting until something reads the directory instead' was itself 19 days stale when read. A pointer cannot rot because nothing is stored to go stale.
